content.comment_body: Hello, I'm trying to add a "Reset Button" that restores default parameter values in my program. This is useful if an operator changes settings and then can't recall the original values. In this setup, the operator can change the parameters through the LCD screen of the [product_name]. Has anyone created a similar program with [product_name]? I've attached a prototype of my program. Thanks in advance.
Could you clarify what your specific question is? Are you just asking if someone else has implemented this solution?
My program isn't working—I need to reset parameter values to their defaults with a button. Is that clearer?
No, it's not clear because I don't see comments or message text in your program. Using an analog multiplexer is the correct approach.

You could copy the original program with default values to a microSD card and insert it into your [product_name]. Install an ON-OFF switch for the power. Each time you turn the device off and back on, it loads the original program with default values from the SD card.
What happens if there's a power failure? Then the [product_name] reads the program from the SD card, which may not be what you want.

The issue is that the value at the MUX is switched only temporarily with an edge. You need to store the toggle edge, which then switches the MUX. It’s also necessary to request a new value from the user for changes and reset memory when the value is updated.
Hello [user_name], I think your suggestion might cause other issues.

The idea is for the default value to load as soon as the Reset button is pressed. In my program, the value isn't stored in block B002 after pressing Reset. Some controllers solve this using a MOVE function. Are you familiar with that? How can I perform MOVE operation within a [product_name]?
What you're doing with the signal edge is essentially a MOVE function, but in your case it's only temporary.
Unusual suggestion: Use a counter. Check the attached notes for details.
Same issue occurs during a power failure—the system resets to the default start value. Is that what you want to happen?
With respect, I disagree. Or is the simulation incorrect?
Hello [user_name], Sorry, that was my mistake. You're right—a up/down counter is also an effective solution.
Hello @[user_name], Thanks for the ingenious counter-based solution. It's practical and straightforward. I also appreciate everyone else's input. Thanks again and have a great weekend!

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking for an easy and dependable way to reset default parameter values on the [product_name] after modifications made via the LCD interface. Since a direct 'Reset to Default' function is missing, users discuss various complex alternatives such as manual programming with MUX blocks and using a microSD card to reload the program—neither solution is as straightforward as desired. This thread highlights user confusion around programming options, challenges with reliably persisting reset values, and uncertainty concerning data memory operations in [product_name] programming.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope for a simple and robust way to reset all parameters to default values using a dedicated reset button on [product_name], similar to features available in other controllers.
